items.title: Albert Morgan Interview, 1958-08-19
items.q: Hinton, uh, no, yeah. After I left, Hinton took my place, because I was right here in California. ... That was my first big band.

ctx.x: Who's the other bass player? Is Rhythm in New York now? Oh, Hinton. Milton Hinton, yeah.
I was confused. I knew he was Rhythm. I couldn't remember.

items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I was afraid to talk to him because he was just too great. But I’d stand, when his show was over I’d stand out by the curb and see how a bass player conducted himself.

ctx.x: Al Morgan. He looked like he was almost seven foot tall. And immaculate. And always immaculate. And I was afraid to talk to him because he was just too great. But I’d stand, when his show was over I’d stand out by the curb and see how a bass player conducted himself. And he come out all sharply dressed and the ladies would ask him for his autograph, and he’d write autographs over there, and he would write his autograph on a © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

piece of paper, and he’d reach in his pocket and pull out a sheet of stamps, and tear one off, and put it on his autograph. And I said, “Wow, man. If I get ever so — one day I will do that.” I haven’t made it yet, but — give me a sheet of stamps. But he was wonderful. And how I got the gig was they went to California to do this movie with Al Jolson, “The Singing Kid.” And Al Jolson was so great, I mean Al Morgan was so great and he had such photogenic features and things, that Cab looked around and the camera was…

items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was replacing this very great Al Morgan... in Cab Calloway's band

ctx.x: A little bit because in intermission we played pinochle and he put a big light behind him and he put the cards up like this. He put them all in place and he didn‟t look at them again. You just say ten of Jack, ten of spades and if he had the jack, he‟d put the jack on it. But I‟m working and Cab Calloway is making his first trip with [Unintelligible] to California where Al Jolson, the same kid from the movie… Ben Webster‟s in Cab Calloway‟s band. He‟s got this great band and a fabulous bass player, Al Morgan,…
